metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., -0.70 or lower) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% relative to prior high.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast at 1.5x prior peak or use 30-day moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending upward, model often underestimates the next 5–7 day move — add 2–3% buffer to forecast if sentiment > 0.50.
- Model consistently overestimates 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed or neutral — apply 3–5% downward adjustment if sentiment < 0.20.
- Mean reversion bias: if price has been above 30-day MA for 5+ days, model tends to overpredict — reduce forecast by 3–7% if sentiment is weak or neutral.
- Overshoot correction: if model forecast exceeds true outcome by >15% in 3 consecutive days, apply “lag correction” — subtract 10–15% from next forecast if sentiment remains unchanged.
